newsitem.title: USA: Eastman Kodak expects strong half for PET.
newsitem.headline: Eastman Kodak expects strong half for PET.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co expects a strong second half from its Eastapak PET polyester packaging plastics, chief executive Earnest Davenport Jr. said Monday.

Reporting second quarter earnings last month -- of $1.14 per share, down from the year earlier $1.41 but up 25 percent from the first quarter -- the company said: "The improvement over the previous two quarters is primarily a result of increased volume and improving prices for our Eastapak PET polyester packaging plastics," lower costs for petrochemical feedstocks and cost cutting efforts.
"PET prices are holding quite well," Davenport said in an interview, noting "a little softening in Europe."
Overall, he said, prices are holding, with the exception of fibers.
He also said Industrial Intermediates are expected to have a stronger second quarter as prices rise.

Davenport said two warning flags of possible problems later in the half would be deterioration of the PET supply-demand balance as new capacity comes on line, and the failure of fibers volume to come back as expected.
